category_title: Students with emotional and behavioural disabilities transitioning to mainstream vocational settings
minimal_context: Ian is in a mainstream woodworking class where he is supposed to be working on the construction of a side table.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You need to start working on the construction of your side table. Who are you?

STUDENT: My name’s Ian.

TUTOR: Ian, you need to get to work on your semester-long independent project.

STUDENT: I'm not doing it. It's towards the end of term and I've missed classes.

TUTOR: You still have to do the work.

STUDENT: (Fails to start working) I'm unable to complete my project anyway, so I'm not doing it.

options.A: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions with the student instead of imposing control.
options.B: Have a student learning support officer attend the mainstream woodworking class with the student.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task during the woodworking class.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for the side table project during the woodworking class.
